feed.title: Editors, IDEs & Terminals — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Apache NetBeans
entry.summary: A multi-language open-source IDE, strong for Java.

entry.title: Awesome CLI
entry.summary: A list gathering useful, small command-line tools. Unlike broad lists such as awesome-shell, it focuses on small single-purpose tools you can install and use right away.

entry.title: Awesome Git Addons
entry.summary: A list of add-on commands and tools that enhance the git CLI. Unlike git clients, it collects not GUIs but tools that add new subcommands to `git`.

entry.title: Awesome Hyper
entry.summary: A list of themes and plugins for Hyper, the web-tech terminal.

entry.title: Awesome Neovim
entry.summary: A list of plugins and configurations for the Neovim editor. Unlike Vim plugin lists, it gathers plugins written in Lua that rely on Neovim-only features such as Tree-sitter and LSP.

entry.title: Awesome VS Code
entry.summary: A list of extensions and resources for Visual Studio Code. Unlike the Marketplace itself it is curated: instead of thousands of extensions, it groups proven ones by language and task.

entry.title: Cmder
entry.summary: A portable, pleasant console package for Windows that ships with bash and unix commands. Unlike the built-in cmd it offers tabs, themes and unix tools together.

entry.title: Editor.md
entry.summary: An open-source, in-browser Markdown editor with live preview and export.

entry.title: hub
entry.summary: A wrapper extending the git command line with GitHub operations (PRs, issues, forks).

entry.title: Hyper
entry.summary: An open-source terminal built with web technologies and extensible via plugins.

entry.title: Micro
entry.summary: A modern, intuitive terminal-based text editor with familiar shortcuts.

entry.title: Neovim
entry.summary: A refactored Vim where configuration and plugins are written in Lua and language-server (LSP) support is built in. Unlike classic Vim, it has that Lua ecosystem and an asynchronous plugin architecture.

entry.title: ranwhen
entry.summary: A tool that visualises when your system was running, right in the terminal.

entry.title: Sublime Text
entry.summary: A text/code editor focused on speed and fluidity, opening very fast.

entry.title: Visual Studio Code
entry.summary: The most widely used code editor: it starts light but approaches an IDE through language servers and debuggers. Unlike full IDEs such as JetBrains, every language comes as an extension — a small base with capability added on.

entry.title: Eclipse Theia
entry.summary: An IDE framework that runs on the desktop and in the browser and takes VS Code extensions. The difference from VS Code is that it is a framework rather than a product — built for you to construct your own IDE on top of.

entry.title: Notepad++
entry.summary: A lightweight source editor for Windows with syntax highlighting, multi-file search and replace, and macro recording. The reason to reach for it over VS Code is speed: it opens a huge log file in seconds without waiting on a language server.

entry.title: VSCodium
entry.summary: A community build of VS Code with Microsoft’s telemetry and branding stripped out. Same editor, same extension API; the difference is that the default marketplace is Open VSX rather than Microsoft’s, so some proprietary extensions are simply absent.

entry.title: Warp
entry.summary: A terminal written in Rust that keeps each command and its output as a separate block instead of one scrolling stream, so you can copy a single command’s output in one click. That block model and the built-in AI command suggestions are what set it apart.

entry.title: WakaTime
entry.summary: Measures how long you spend in which project and language through an editor plugin. Against general time trackers it needs no manual start — the measurement comes from the editor itself.

entry.title: fli
entry.summary: Brings flight search to the command line, and because results are scriptable you can hang price tracking off a cron job.

entry.title: Embarcadero Dev-C++
entry.summary: A lightweight C/C++ IDE. Behind modern ones, yet it runs on weak hardware and remains the standard install in many Turkish university labs.
